page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8y.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs based on the 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64), utilizing Alibaba's custom Yitian710 processor running at 2.75 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 physical cores and a single thread per core, backed by 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard computing tasks. The instance achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1819.78 and a multi-core score of 7230.46. Memory read bandwidth is measured at 407.26 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 63.39 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. However, write bandwidth for large uncached blocks is weaker at 25.44 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance is a notable bottleneck, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 10% at 659.83, despite the presence of AES hardware acceleration. Large-model LLM inference is also limited, with 7B model text generation performing poorly at 4.54 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the arm64-based architecture offers a balanced resource density of 4 GB RAM per vCPU, making it a viable option for workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores without the premium of x86 licensing. Given its performance profile, the instance is appropriate for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, text processing, and moderate database operations. It is less suitable for memory-write intensive tasks, heavy cryptography, or complex vector-based computations due to the absence of AVX and AMX instruction sets.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8y.xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs on the 2.75 GHz Alibaba Yitian710 processor, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM and 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks place the instance in the average tier for single-core and multi-core CPU tasks, software compilation, and static web serving. However, it exhibits weaker performance in uncached memory write operations and scores in the bottom 10% for CPU encryption tests. Lacking AVX and AMX instruction sets, it is not designed for advanced vector math. The instance is best utilized for general-purpose workloads, including text processing, light database operations, and web serving, offering a balanced resource profile for ARM-native applications.
